description: A desktop app for macOS and Linux for managing projects — each one lead agent the user talks to, with a team of persistent agent sessions behind it — powered by installed agent CLIs.
features: Project workspaces: delegating lead, liaison card, layer teammates on demand, openable teammate/liaison chats with direct talk, Stop/Refresh controls, unstaffed chips, single-open guard
Home workspace agent: finds projects by name, opens them, hands their leads a first prompt
Any harness verbatim: Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, ACP, per-chat model/effort/permissions
Streaming markdown replies: tool chips, inline diffs, read previews, unified permission cards
App-side prompt queue: reorder, merge with undo, edit, interrupt, holds on connection/limit errors
Attachments: images, videos, PDFs, files, region crops, viewer, sketch pad
Edit and rewind: per-harness checkpoints, outside chats brought in as teammates, lost-session auto fresh-start with resend, startup-failure auto-retry
Subagents and background scripts as live cards, agents page, brief-started agents
Agent messaging with interrupt-or-queue delivery, busy status, jobs handed to another project's lead (ask_project), per-project rules, approvals
Bridge preview and takeover for web pages via hidden CDP browser and native apps via Accessibility (macOS) or X11 + AT-SPI over D-Bus (Linux)
MCP servers, plugins, marketplaces for Claude Code and Codex via Settings

Project memory as an audited log, folded from every finished turn and checked against the code, with project-wide recall by words and meaning, git state block, layered architecture sheets with per-layer session notes and slim project-wide catchup
Sessions edit layer sheets only after reading, by line number with stale-read guard
Frontend component library with freshness stamps, auto-refresh and picture capture
Self-compaction at half-window: handoff note, owed letters carried forward
Linux: per-user make install, GNOME app grid entry, Ctrl for ⌘ shortcuts, no grants to ask for

Stable self-signed `ruri dev` identity keeps privacy grants across rebuilds

conversation.summary: This layer is the conversation surface: composing prompts in Composer.tsx and reading replies in ChatPane.tsx as grouped transcript turns. Rendering is componentized per event kind (EventView, Exchange, Diff, Thinking, Questions) with markdown sanitized to HTML and code highlighting cached plus offloaded to a worker. A newcomer must grasp that the prompt is plain text with markers ([image #n], /commands) mirrored as chips, and the transcript is a flat event stream grouped into turns at render time.

map.name: Attachment chips, viewer and region crops
Carry-on after an agent compacted itself

flows.name: Send a prompt
steps: Type plain text with markers in Composer.tsx textarea
Markers parsed and mirrored as chips via lib/markers.ts and Markers.tsx
Attachments and sketch images appended with region crops from Attachments.tsx
Slash command resolved via CommandMenu.tsx and scripts/commands.ts
Sent through store send; ChatPane.tsx groups reply events into turns via Exchange.tsx groupTurns

flows.name: Render a reply
steps: ChatPane.tsx receives flat TranscriptEvent stream
Exchange.tsx groupTurns folds user prompt through following events; compaction stands solo
EventView.tsx renders each event kind with shortened paths and command chips
Markdown goes through lib/markdownHtml.ts with DOMPurify then markdown.tsx components
Code blocks highlight inline or via highlight.worker.ts with cache in highlighter.ts

flows.name: Answer a question
steps: Ask/permission event renders QuestionCard in Questions.tsx or PermissionBanner.tsx
One question shown at a time with slide navigation and persisted picks
Answer sent back in harness-native shape via store send

rules: Never put highlighting or sanitizing inline in components: markdown goes via lib/markdownHtml.ts with DOMPurify since model output is untrusted innerHTML.
Do not re-highlight from scratch: highlighter.ts caches by language plus text and only long blocks go to highlight.worker.ts; short blocks stay inline.
Keep markers as text: find, move, space and strip them only with lib/markers.ts so mirror width and wrapping stay identical to the textarea.
Compaction events are solo turns in groupTurns and never fold or host other events.
Sketch keeps shapes and redraws at export size with per-channel autosave; it closes only on its own close button, never on Escape.

A user event whose text opens with CARRY_ON (shared handoffNote) is ruri's carry-on after a self-compaction: render it as CarryOn, never as the user's bubble or as a letter from its `from` (with `carried` that only says whose job it still is); server continuePrompt must keep opening with CARRY_ON.

navigation-projects.summary: This layer moves the user between projects: a sidebar row per project (its lead behind it, the count of teammates at work beside it), HomeBoard projects overview, ⌘K/right-Option Switcher, per-chat Queue list, Rapid Fire line, SessionControls pickers, and Player music bar. It is built as presentational React components over the app store (useRuri/send) plus three small libs (fuzzy scoring, run-note staleness, Web Audio engine). Newcomers must grasp that a project is one chat for the user, its lead; its team's members never show here as their own rows, and these components navigate and display state but never own turn execution.

Team-at-work dragon and count (row and Projects row)

Unread pips and recent-note lines update from store (teammates' turns wear none)

rules: HomeBoard never animates: streaming reply words and anything moving belong only to the open chat.

A project's team never shows here: the sidebar, switcher, rapid fire line and projects board give each project once, as its lead (leadOf), and setActive sends a member's id to its lead. RapidFire must not move the app's active session; leaving the line returns to where the user was.

appearance-library.summary: Appearance owns ruri's look: light/dark/ember theming, the sidebar peek band, the empty-chat hero face, the dragon usage gauges, and the shared UI pieces (dropdown, confirm, settings rows). It is built as pure presentational state plus editors — shape/parse helpers in lib, live window copies in band.ts/hero.ts/pictures.ts, and manga-styled components. A newcomer must grasp that band/hero are stored shapes read back checked from disk, with live bytes and animation state kept separately, and that a visible window keeps animating whether or not it has focus.

app-shell.summary: This layer is the web app shell: entry HTML, React root, global zustand store with socket wiring, local-first prefs, and global manga-theme styles. It freezes a window nobody can see (minimised, hidden, another Space, or fully covered — not merely unfocused): inbound updates are held with only the latest kept and applied in one redraw on wake, while agents and terminals keep running. It also carries the Linux shell adaptations: Permissions settings renders a no-grants message instead of macOS calls and shortcuts use Ctrl on Linux. Newcomers must grasp that store.ts is the single state/socket hub all feature layers read, that held.ts owns the asleep hold-and-catch-up, and that styles.css plus the beat/awake/spin clocks define how anything may look or move.

main.tsx paints cached pref theme then mounts web/src/App.tsx

clocks in web/src/lib/beat.ts and web/src/lib/spin.ts start only while awake per web/src/lib/awake.ts

steps: window sleeps and store sets live false
web/src/lib/held.ts holds inbound updates keeping only the latest of each kind
server holds chat streams at the marked position
on wake held updates apply in a single redraw
server sends each open chat exactly what it missed

rules: No CSS animations for ambient motion — drive steps from lib/beat.ts or lib/spin.ts so Chromium composites one layer instead of repainting at display rate.

Never touch the DOM when a tick changes nothing, and never move anything while asleep, out of view, or under prefers-reduced-motion. Asleep means unseen (document.hidden), never merely unfocused — a visible window that slept on blur froze chats mid-reply; focus only sets the peek band's drag region (data-unfocused).
A pref set this session wins over an arriving server snapshot — do not let hydrate overwrite touched keys.
Surfaces differ by shade, never by line or shadow: keep --edge invisible and use --rim for genuine frames.
Tuner page and tuner-save endpoint are dev-only and must never enter the app bundle or production build.
Fixture mode is screenshots and timing only — it never talks to a server or spends tokens.

chat-runs-queue.summary: This layer runs live chat turns: prompt dispatch, the app-side queue, turn progress and transcript delivery over the socket, and the team and talk built on them. A prompt is written, checkpointed, titled, and queued or run; every agent sees its context use and compacts itself past half its window through a handoff-note continuation queued at the head; a finished turn drains the queue or retries.

map.name: self-compaction (context line, compact/context tools, handoff-note continuation)
agent-to-agent talk and project teams (lead, liaison, members, the leads' team tools and what a lead is refused, team message liaison and freeLayers)

flows.name: prompt to running turn
steps: handlers/prompts.ts accepts send, split, stop, or queue rearrange
dispatch.ts writes prompt to transcript, checkpoints, titles, splits slash commands
queue.ts holds it if channel busy, visible or silent entry
chats.ts hands it to the chat session with briefing and tools
turns.ts tracks progress and context during the run
events.ts records, redacts, archives, and pushes each event
finished turn triggers drainQueue and maybeRetry in dispatch.ts

flows.name: self-compact mid-job
steps: each prompt carries a usage line (used / window / self-compact point); any agent can check with the context tool
past its point the agent writes a handoff note and calls the compact tool, which only stores the note and tells it to end its turn
at that turn's result in chats.ts, an ok result queues the continuation at the head and runs the compaction, whose drain sends it into the fresh session
a stopped turn drops the note and settles letters as today; a failed turn keeps the note for the next ok turn
if the compacting turn was answering a letter, its letter is carried to the continuation so its last words still answer whoever waits

flows.name: rewind
steps: handlers/rewind.ts receives rewind to just before a prompt ran
restoreContext resets context gauge to the kept exchange
files and repo restored via native fork or checkpoint plus brief
transcript truncated and prompt returned to composer

flows.name: talk message
steps: handlers/talk.ts finds the seat — the sender's own team, or another project's door: its liaison, made on first outside contact — and checks TalkPolicy (mayMessage)
delivered as a prompt marked whose (only RURI_TEAM_MAX makes a sleeping member waitForSlot)
queues behind that chat's work, or cuts in

at turn end its last word goes back to the sender, unless the turn handed the job on (Pending.for): then the turn the last answer starts (LetterFrom.owes) answers; ask_project goes to another project's liaison
sending a letter refreshes an open team page for both ends so liaison letters show live

rules: Split sub-prompts ride silent under the original prompt; split only when reaching the front so earlier commands run first.
An entry being rewritten keeps queue place but nothing sends it until the rewrite returns.
Only existing commands count — ruri's own, harness prompt commands, installed skills; quoted ones ('/compact', "/compact", `/compact`) and /tmp alone on a line stay plain text to the model.
RURI_TEAM_MAX, when set, caps members at work; one holding on an answer (talk.awaiting) doesn't count, or mutual waits hold every slot for good. Only waking a sleeping member is gated.
Turn progress lives in turns.ts not the window so the clock survives reload; broadcast deltas throttled to one message a second.
Rewind must restore files, branch, transcript, composer prompt, and context gauge to the kept exchange, not the tip.

A letter is answered by the last words of the turn that finishes the job: owedLetter() is what a turn owes (its own letter, a carried one, or via an answer's owes); talkTurnEnded settles it only when nothing sent for it is out (TalkBook.outstanding). An answer that leaves the book any other way — a wait in another job, taken out of the queue — goes through answerOnward. Self-compaction marks the carry (carryLetter) at the turn's result, before talkTurnEnded.

The liaison (session.liaison) is never marked lead and leadOf skips it; it is not a member either: what takes 'every non-lead session' as the team must skip it (membersOf, store.isMember, protocol isMember); unattended() covers members and the liaison, whose held lines nobody sends on by hand.

A lead's or the liaison's Edit/Write/NotebookEdit/Agent/Task are refused by a PreToolUse hook naming whom to hand the job to (SessionExtras.refuse), never disallowedTools: its bare 'No such tool' sent mira's lead into Bash. headWatch (afterTools) nudges at a writing or running command, or every third look.
edges: Protocol — every socket message and transcript event is typed in shared/protocol.ts
Agent harnesses — dispatch and chats hand prompts to sessions and get turns, checkpoints, and forks back
Projects, memory and history — checkpoints, compaction, handoff briefs, notes, and archive feed prompts, rewind, and events
Server runtime and transport — socket routing, clients push, uploads, and stores carry transcript and queue messages
Conversation — composer sends and queue/transcript handlers drive what the chat pane shows

projects-memory-history.summary: This layer owns project sessions and everything remembered about them: sessions/chats in projects.json, live transcripts plus history with stable exchange numbers, per-prompt file checkpoints, the project memory, project-wide recall, and the .ruri briefs and sheets. The memory is an append-only event log per project (memory/<id>.jsonl) whose current lines are written to briefs.json; every finished turn is folded in by the memory model as ops, and each line is checked against the code it names. A newcomer must grasp the split: the live session file is rewritten per event, history JSONL is append-only by compaction, the memory changes only through its log, briefs are assembled at send time without calling a model, leads are pure delegators with a hidden liaison for cross-project work, and every agent now compacts itself at half its window with its own handoff note while ruri's 80% compaction stays as backstop.

map.name: Projects (open/close/rename/star/hide), leads and the hidden liaison, and their teams' members (stop/refresh/restart/retire, closeMember, the one teardown forgetChat)
Compaction, digests, auto-compact, self-compaction and carried delegations
Memory log, folds and the check against the code
Project brief / architecture sheet and lead/liaison briefings

flows.name: Compact and resume
steps: past the harness's share of the window at turn end (0.8; Gemini 0.6), or by the user, or by the agent itself past half its window via mcp__ruri__compact with its own note
compactChannel (server/dispatch.ts)
server/archive.ts appends live events to history JSONL, keeps exchange numbers, retires the live session

brief built at send within 10k tokens, no model call (server/compaction.ts, server/handoff.ts); when Claude compacts itself, its PreCompact/SessionStart hooks (server/sessions.ts) get afterCompactBrief and the sheet-read guard resets
self-compact continuation queued at head of line then drained into the fresh session (server/selfCompaction.ts); thin notes, early requests, and immediate re-compacts refused
a continuation answering a delegated letter keeps the same letter id with carried: true, carried via carryLetter in the result branch before talk turn-end

flows.name: Checkpoint and rewind
steps: server/checkpoints.ts captures whole working tree into git via private index under refs/ruri/ once per prompt send and once per turn end
ref named for prompt; user branch, staging area and git log untouched
rewind reads refs to undo what a chat's turns did, reported as RewindReport

flows.name: Remember and recall
steps: turn end
enqueueFold (server/memoryQueue.ts)
memory model returns ADD/UPDATE/SUPERSEDE/RETIRE/NOOP ops (server/memoryFold.ts)
MemoryBook.apply (server/memoryLog.ts) appends events, writes current lines to briefs.json
server/memoryCheck.ts checks anchors (server/grounding.ts); a verifier confirms, supersedes or retires
ruri recall and the brief's pick fuse BM25, trigram and embeddings by RRF across the project (server/projectSearch.ts, server/retrieval.ts)

files: server/projects.ts — ProjectStore over projects.json plus per-chat session settings; a project's lead first and its members with duty and layers, plus the hidden liaison session (formTeams at launch, addMember, setMember)
server/handlers/projects.ts — socket moves for projects, a member off its team (closeMember), an outside chat brought in as a teammate
server/archive.ts — live sessions/<id>.json plus append-only history/<id>.jsonl and turn summaries
server/checkpoints.ts — per-prompt hidden git commits and rewind
server/compaction.ts — briefs within the token budget, state lines, anchored digest sections
server/selfCompaction.ts — agent self-compact notes, threshold checks and continuation into the fresh session
server/memoryLog.ts — the memory event log: actor rules, caps that archive, undo, reconcile with briefs.json; fed by server/memoryQueue.ts, checked by server/memoryCheck.ts
server/projectSearch.ts — project-wide hybrid search over exchanges and memory lines (BM25 in server/recall.ts)
server/catchupBrief.ts — sheet broadcast and rebuild from app side
rules: Nothing except compaction appends to history/<id>.jsonl; live session file is the only rewritten transcript.
Checkpoints must use a private index file and refs/ruri/ refs; never touch the user's staging area, branch, or pushed refs.

The memory changes only through MemoryBook.apply (server/memoryLog.ts), never by writing briefs.json: a line a fold leaves out stays; the model edits only its own lines; agent lines go only with a reason and evidence; user and pinned lines are never touched by the model; cap overflow archives.

Building and sending a brief calls no model and never waits on one (embeddings count only if already warmed; the digest folds in the background), and the system-prompt briefing stays byte-stable so the prompt cache holds — anything dynamic (<state>, <memory-update>) rides in the prompt.

Only sessions ruri did not start are offered by recent import, and one brought in joins the team as a named member (addMember) — never re-import one of ruri's own chats. A project's chats change only through its team: no new, close or rename moves, and a lead goes only with its project.
Exchange numbers are stable (seqs/nextSeq in server/archive.ts); refs and turn files use them, never a position.

The compact tool only stores the note and tells the model to end its turn; it never stops the turn itself. Compaction runs at that turn's result: ok compacts with the continuation, stopped drops the note and settles the letter as today, failed keeps the note for the next ok turn.

A self-compact continuation answering a letter keeps the same letter id with carried: true on its from; carryLetter is called in the result branch at selfCompactDue time, never inside the tool call, or a stopped turn leaves the letter hanging.
edges: Chat runs and queue — supplies prompts, turns, events and rewind entry points this layer archives and checkpoints
Protocol — TranscriptEvent, TurnSummary, MemoryLine, Project/Session and brief sheet types in shared/protocol.ts
Server runtime and transport — routing, auth, uploads and stores hosting projects/handlers endpoints

Agent harnesses — session ids resumed; the memory model's lane (completeMemory in server/smallmodel.ts); Claude's PreCompact/SessionStart hooks and the PostToolBatch hook that tells it its context mid-turn (SessionExtras.contextNotice, server/sessions.ts)
Library, skills and sweeps — sweep/describe candidates feed catchup; library owns skill removal on teardown

library-skills-sweeps.summary: This layer keeps each project's component library — user names, handles, code refs, and screenshots — plus repo-wide naming sweeps and harness skills. The store is server/components.ts with the agent CLI in server/library.ts; handlers, refresh, screenshots, sweeps, and skills orbit it. Newcomer idea: the filesystem and git are truth — this layer indexes, names, and photographs what exists, never renders it.

flows.name: Register and reuse a component
steps: Agent builds UI and registers it via server/library.ts (ruri register) into server/components.ts store
server/handlers/components.ts hosts naming card and stores shot via storeShot
Later agent searches with ruri search/show and copies with planCopy/installCommand
server/libraryRefresh.ts marks entry changed/stale as files move

flows.name: Sweep and photograph a repo
steps: server/sweep.ts skims source tops, exports, CSS classes for candidates
Names proposed and written via server/components.ts index
server/shots.ts boots dev server and captures selector rectangles
Unreachable entries go to agent photo chat via server/photographer.ts prompt

flows.name: Skills management
steps: server/skills.ts scans global and project skill dirs
server/handlers/skills.ts pushes list and serves bodies
toggle moves folder to skills-off/, install/remove/update shell out to bmo

files: server/components.ts — per-project component index, store, mention detection, model tools
server/library.ts — agent ruri CLI: search/show/add/register, copy planning, arg parsing
server/handlers/components.ts — app-side host, naming tools, refresh orchestration, library endpoint
server/sweep.ts — repo skim naming pass for unnamed UI files
server/libraryRefresh.ts — git-based staleness: renames, deletions, changes since last seen
server/shots.ts — dev-server boot and selector screenshot capture via CaptureHost
server/skills.ts — filesystem-backed skill listing, toggle via skills-off, bmo shell-outs

server/handlers/skills.ts — skills page messages, command menu data, pushSkills
rules: Never invent components or screenshots: files, selectors, and pictures must be observed from source or a running app.
Entries drift — always consult libraryRefresh changes/tidyFiles and ComponentStore.touch semantics before trusting notes or shots.
Do not delete on skill disable: park to skills-off/ so bmo metadata and updates survive.
Shots cannot cover login-gated, state-dependent, or non-web UI — route those to photographer agent flow, not shots.ts.
edges: Protocol — NamedComponent, ComponentProposal, Attachment, SkillInfo types in shared/protocol.ts
Server runtime and transport — uploads storedFilePath, config/ruri dirs, dispatch, channel project resolution
Bridge / Desktop shell — CaptureHost loads URLs in hidden window and captures element rectangles
Agent harnesses — smallmodel naming pass feeds sweep; harnesses consume skills and library via ruri CLI

terminals-agents-integrations.summary: This layer runs everything beside the chat turn: composer pty terminals, background script output, user-started crew agents, folder-backed music serving, and harness integrations plus host/settings plumbing. It is built as small stateful server modules (Terminals, TerminalRelay, Scrollback, PrefStore) fronted by thin socket handlers, with CLI-mediated side effects. Newcomers must grasp that terminals are paced append-streams with backpressure, and integration changes apply only at next harness launch.

flows.name: Terminal output to windows
steps: Terminals spawns login shell on pty via expect (pipes fallback)
Chunks appended to Scrollback in O(arrival) pieces
TerminalRelay holds per-window queue; ready window gets chunk at once
Behind windows coalesce waiting chunks into one message on drain
All windows behind pauses pty reads so writer blocks; nothing buffers unbounded

flows.name: Integration change
steps: Window reads via readIntegrations (file listings, never starts servers)
Change runs through harness CLI command (e.g. claude mcp add-json)
Warm sessions on changed harness retired as each goes idle
Next prompt starts fresh process with new servers/plugins

flows.name: Crew agent run
steps: Chat agents page starts agent on its own SessionManager
Card moves along; log holds brief and run output
agent_send follows up on same conversation; agent_stop ends long run
Chat transcript and status hear none of it

files: server/terminal.ts — real pty shells per channel/tab behind composer terminal mode
server/relay.ts — paces shell output to windows with per-window queues and pty backpressure
server/scrollback.ts — chunk-list scrollback, joined only on read
server/handlers/terminal.ts — socket handlers for terminal list/new/open/input/resize/close
server/handlers/crew.ts — user-started crew agents on their own session manager
server/scripts.ts — background script output page read from harness output file tail
server/integrations.ts — MCP/plugin/marketplace read and CLI-mediated changes
server/handlers/integrations.ts — Integrations settings handlers; retires warm sessions on change
server/music.ts — folder-as-playlist music library scan and same-origin track serving
server/prefs.ts — machine-scoped untyped window preference bag
rules: Never write a harness config format by hand; every integration change goes through that CLI's own command.
Never health-check Claude servers with `claude mcp list`; it starts every server — read ~/.claude.json / .mcp.json / plugin lists instead.
Keep integration secrets as names only here; values stay in the harness layer.
Terminal output is append-only so coalescing is safe; do not reorder or drop chunks.
New window preferences need no change in server/prefs.ts — it is a deliberately untyped bag (max 200 keys).
edges: Agent harnesses — integration changes take effect only when a harness next starts; warm sessions retired idle
Bridge — host handlers reach desktop shell for picker, permissions, bridge windows; no-ops headless
Protocol — tabs, permissions, playlists, crew cards, integration rows typed in shared/protocol.ts
Server runtime and transport — music served over /music/* same-origin; prefs/config live machine-side

server-runtime-transport.summary: This layer is the Node HTTP + WebSocket transport everything else rides on: one port serving the UI, uploads, and the socket every window talks over. It is built around a single shared ServerContext (server/context.ts) assembled once in server/server.ts and handed to routes, socket, and handlers. A newcomer must grasp: this layer moves bytes and enforces origin/token gates — domain logic lives in handlers and other layers, not here — it also carries each agent's context-usage line and self-compact request path with continuation queueing and owed-answer routing, now with a CARRY_ON-prefixed continuation prompt detected by its opening text, and a window only sleeps when it cannot be seen at all (minimized, on another Space, or fully covered); a visible-but-unfocused window stays live and keeps receiving streams. It also serves the team status behind the team page: liaison state with current work/answering/waiting-on rows, free-layer chips, Stop/Refresh semantics, and an optional machine cap only when RURI_TEAM_MAX is set.

flows.name: Window connects and stays live
steps: HTTP server from server/routes.ts and socket from server/socket.ts listen on one claimed port (server/port.ts)
Socket upgrade checked for page origin and token (server/auth.ts), rejected otherwise
New client registered with its on-screen view (server/clients.ts)
Snapshot of everything sent on connect, then per-chat transcript only to windows showing it

A window reports live:false only when unseen (minimized, another Space, fully covered) and then its chat streams are gated off and other updates held latest-only; a visible-but-unfocused window stays live; on wake it catches up in one redraw plus per-chat missed content
Each incoming message schema-checked and handed to server/handlers/index.ts

flows.name: Attachment upload and serve-back
steps: Base64 upload received over HTTP or socket
Persisted under config uploads dir with sanitized unique path (server/uploads.ts)
Transcript carries small /uploads/<file> URL instead of base64
Served back via serveUpload with MIME from server/mime.ts
Stale files reaped by scripts/uploads-sweep.ts

flows.name: Mutating request gate
steps: Route or socket handler asks server/auth.ts for originAllowed and tokenMatches
GETs stay open; POSTs need token plus permitted origin
Token file written 0600 and removed on close (scripts/auth.ts, scripts/lib/server.ts)
Failed checks rejected before any store or handler runs

flows.name: Agent self-compaction
steps: Every prompt carries a usage line (used/of threshold) from catchUp in server/handoff.ts (contextLine, server/selfCompaction.ts), repeated mid-turn on PostToolBatch; agent can query mcp__ruri__context or {"do":"context"} on /talk/<id>

Past threshold the agent calls mcp__ruri__compact or {"do":"compact","note"|"file"} (server/routes.ts, server/handlers/talk.ts, shared/protocol.ts); tool only stores the note and tells the model to end its turn, it does not stop the turn
At that turn's result in server/chats.ts, selfCompactDue returns the note; carryLetter is called then, before talkTurnEnded, so a stopped turn drops the note and settles the letter as today
Continuation is queued at the head (server/queue.ts) then compactChannel runs and its drain sends it into the fresh session
Continuation prompt starts with CARRY_ON via continuePrompt (server/selfCompaction.ts) and is detected by that opening text plus handoffNote() in shared/protocol.ts, so old transcripts still match
Transcript shows a compacted-itself line plus the handoff note bubble; a carried continuation keeps the same letter id with carried:true so the owed answer still routes back

files: server/server.ts — assembles stores, managers, timers, routes and socket on one port
server/context.ts — the shared ServerContext object every part takes first
server/routes.ts — HTTP side: health, uploads, static UI, origin/token-gated mutations
server/socket.ts — WebSocket upgrade gate, snapshot on connect, schema-checked dispatch
server/clients.ts — per-window views and targeted transcript/status broadcast
server/auth.ts — origin and token checks for HTTP and socket
server/selfCompaction.ts — self-compact threshold, note validation and due check
server/chats.ts — turn result branch running self-compact and continuation queueing
server/uploads.ts — attachment persist, model payload, serve and sweep
server/handlers/team.ts — team actions (stop/refresh/restart/compact/retire) and liaison/free-layer status
rules: Never put domain logic in routes/socket — dispatch to server/handlers/index.ts; what each message does lives per-domain.
Never weaken the gate: mutating HTTP needs token + permitted origin, socket needs both at upgrade; GETs stay open.
The port is identity (origin for stored prefs) — claim it via server/port.ts, never silently fall to an ephemeral port.

Transcript fan-out is scoped: live per-chat events go only to windows showing that chat (server/clients.ts); the snapshot and the projects page carry only Home's and the leads' tails (ProjectStore.leadIds) — a team's members are never sent whole, though a window (or a test script) may still view one by id

Persist carefully: uploads as URL-backed files, never inline base64 in transcript events; every store fixes its config folder when it is made, so a put-off write lands where the store was read — and bun test preloads a folder of its own (bunfig.toml, scripts/test-config.ts), so a test run never touches ~/.config/ruri.
Secrets must never enter model context, logs, or transcripts — only names/placeholders leave server/secrets.ts.

The compact tool must not stop the turn or settle the owed letter: call carryLetter in the chats.ts result branch only when selfCompactDue returns a note, still before talkTurnEnded, so a stopped turn drops the note and settles normally.
The server must refuse team actions on the liaison, and stop is only enabled while a teammate's turn is running.
Never show slot/waiting counts unless RURI_TEAM_MAX is set — 'waiting for a slot' can only appear then.
edges: Protocol — every socket message is typed/validated in shared/protocol.ts and shared/clientSchema.ts
Chat runs and queue — handlers under server/handlers/* implement prompt/turn/rewind semantics on top of ServerContext
Agent harnesses — session managers and usage/resource sources (agents, sessions, providers) plug into server.ts assembly
Bridge — HTTP routes proxy bridge pictures/calls via bridge state, not directly; native-app driving needs X11 plus AT-SPI and must refuse on Wayland
Desktop shell — single-instance lock and served UI origin depend on the claimed port

harnesses.summary: This layer drives installed coding CLIs (claude/codex/opencode/gemini/ACP) through yagami's AgentSession/ProviderSession, translating harness events into ruri transcript events. It is built around server/sessions.ts (SessionManager, ~3474 lines) with a provider registry, model catalog, Home manager agent, persistent team subagents with idle sleep/wake and budget gating, auto-updater, and cheap small-model client. Newcomers must grasp: ruri never talks to models directly — every prompt goes through a session object owned here, and transcript/usage/permission shapes are normalized here.

map.name: Small-model summaries, titles and memory folds
Subagent cards, team roster and logs
ACP/OpenCode startup retry (locked DB / dead warm process)
Cross-harness event and session parity checks

flows.name: Prompt turn through a harness
steps: SessionManager builds/resumes provider session in server/sessions.ts
ProviderRegistry resolves harness via server/providers.ts
yagami CLI session streams AgentEvents
sessions.ts normalizes to TranscriptEvents (text, tool chips, patches, questions)
Usage/limits recorded, reply finalized

flows.name: Small-model background call
steps: sessions.ts or memory layer requests title/summary/split
server/smallmodel.ts picks double-starred model, RURI_SMALL_MODEL fallback, then codex default
yagami engine.stream over the signed-in CLI, aborted at a deadline (60s + 20ms/token), stalled model rests and the fallback answers
Result folded back (title, summary, tracker items); skipped when RURI_NO_MEMORY=1

flows.name: Subagent spawn to card
steps: Harness emits spawn/task tool call
sessions.ts creates card with SubagentState
Budget gate admits the teammate (teams capped, one-at-a-time waits for a slot)
Agent work streams to per-agent log in server/agents.ts
Card updates in place; report ends it; idle teammates sleep and wake on message; dead process marked stopped

files: server/sessions.ts — SessionManager: owns AgentSession lifecycle, event-to-transcript translation, permissions, usage
server/providers.ts — ProviderRegistry: creates/loads yagami providers, parses model refs, capability mapping
server/models.ts — Models: startup-probed Claude + harness model picker, live-session replacement
server/smallmodel.ts — cheap completions client for titles, summaries, splits, briefs, tracker extraction
server/manager.ts — Home agent at workspace root with MCP/drop-file tools managing projects
server/agents.ts — per-subagent JSON logs under config agents/<channel>/<key>.json with debounce and cap; team-aware roster, idle sleep/wake and budget gating
server/updater.ts — hourly CLI self-update via native updater/bun/npm/brew, never under a running turn
scripts/provider-events.ts — harness-free fake-provider transcript parity check
scripts/acp-start.ts — ACP restart on closed-pipe/locked-DB startup death
rules: Never bypass SessionManager to call a CLI directly; session resume, permissions and usage accounting live there.
A live session's Claude model report only replaces probed ids/names — never clobber display names resolved from the startup catalog.
Never replace a harness binary mid-turn; updater defers when a chat is active.
Subagent transcript text must never leak into the parent chat — only the card carries SubagentState.

Small-model calls are one per sent prompt and per finished reply, honor RURI_NO_MEMORY=1, and each runs through client.engine.stream with an AbortSignal and a deadline (smallmodel.ts ask) — never messages.create, which takes no signal, so a harness that never answers would keep its process and its place in line for good.
ACP startup failures (locked SQLite, dead warm process) are retried, not surfaced as turn failures.
edges: Chat runs and queue — consumes SessionManager turns and TranscriptEvents over the socket
Projects, memory and history — supplies checkpoints/rewind files and receives small-model summaries, titles, folds
Protocol — every transcript, question, model-choice and subagent message is typed in shared/protocol.ts
Library, skills and sweeps — skills/sweeps feed harness session context and tools
Terminals, agents and integrations — Home manager agent drives app actions via MCP or .ruri/open.jsonl drop file

bridge.summary: This layer lets an agent session see and drive what it built in a hidden window: web pages via the DevTools protocol (CDP) and native apps via CDP (Electron) or the Accessibility tree. It is built as a shared CDP driver in server/cdp.ts plus a tool definition in server/bridge.ts, with Electron-only hands in desktop/bridge.ts, desktop/apps.ts, and desktop/capture.ts. The key idea: the model never touches the user's screen — it gets scaled previews beside the composer while the real window stays hidden and auto-closes after the turn.

map.name: Hidden web page driving (web_open, click, type, screenshot)
Bridge tool definitions and MCP/HTTP briefing
Window lifetime and auto-close after turn
Linux native apps (.desktop lookup, X11 windows and captures, AT-SPI tree and app_ui Python helpers)

flows.name: Drive a hidden web page
steps: Agent calls bridge tool defined in server/bridge.ts
desktop/bridge.ts creates hidden window on first web_open
PageDriver in server/cdp.ts sends CDP verbs over CdpLink (debugger link)
Action result returns scaled preview, not full capture
BridgeState in server/bridgeState.ts schedules close BRIDGE_GRACE_MS after turn ends unless taken over

flows.name: Drive a desktop app
steps: desktop/apps.ts launches Electron with remote-debugging-port or native app with open -g
Electron apps driven over CdpSocket with same PageDriver; native apps driven via Accessibility tree (System Events)
Photographed off window server / compositor without stealing focus
desktop/bridge.ts returns preview and handles quit on session end

flows.name: Capture component targets
steps: desktop/capture.ts loads project page in hidden window
Finds each selector and captures rectangle around it
Refuses blank/collapsed captures
Walks app links (never buttons) to find missing selectors

files: server/cdp.ts — shared CDP driver (CdpLink, CdpSocket, PageDriver) knowing nothing about Electron or sessions
server/bridge.ts — bridge tool definitions, runBridge, MCP/HTTP briefings
desktop/bridge.ts — Electron half: hidden per-channel windows, previews, takeover handling
desktop/apps.ts — background app launch (Electron over CDP, others over Accessibility) and native capture
server/bridgeState.ts — per-channel takeover state and grace-period auto-close after turns
desktop/capture.ts — hidden-window selector screenshot sweep for the component library
desktop/linuxApps.ts — Linux native side: launch without focus (_TIME0 startup id), xdotool windows, X11 captures, AT-SPI over D-Bus from an embedded Python prelude

rules: Nothing in server/cdp.ts may know about Electron, sessions, or the config dir — it stays exercisable without a window.

Never show or activate the driven window: native apps launch with open -g on macOS and a _TIME0 startup id on Linux; a launched Electron app is watched 10s (keepBehind) and handed back whenever its process group is in front, since its window shows on ready-to-show long after attach. Capture works from behind ruri.
Return scaled previews to the model, not full captures.
Hidden windows/apps auto-close a few seconds after the turn ends unless the user took them over; never leave renderers running.
In capture sweeps, follow links only — never click unknown buttons.
Never pin a blank/collapsed screenshot to a component entry.
edges: Desktop shell — owns the visible window, permissions/TCC, and hidden bridge windows that desktop/bridge.ts drives
Protocol — BridgeState type and server messages for previews/takeover live in shared/protocol.ts
Library, skills and sweeps — server/shots.ts starts dev servers and wraps desktop/capture.ts
Agent harnesses — expose server/bridge.ts tools in-process (Claude bridge MCP server) so every harness gets the same verbs
Management: agents, skills and tracking — Bridge preview UI beside the composer and takeover button
